Hi Jonas,

Thanks for agreeing to take a look at our private deployment plan. We are standing up a Redwood Private deployment in our colo footprint (brownfield) and want to validate two things in this review:

1) Network overlay approach — we plan to avoid changing existing VLANs and instead use a lightweight VXLAN overlay with per-tenant VRFs. We included a topology diagram (acme-network-topology-diagram.png).
2) CI golden-path — terraform + helm flows: terraform will manage VPC, subnets, and BGP peerings; helm will deploy the control-plane components. We want a simple CI dry-run (plan/helm template) that gates merging for the initial rollout.

Attachments: acme-brownfield-terraform-plan.diff (terraform plan output), acme-helm-values.yaml

Big questions:
- Is the overlay + VRF pattern in our plan safe from accidental route leaks into tenant VLANs?
- Does our CI gating approach suitably catch drift and prevent secret leakage (we're currently using sealed-secrets + vault)?

Can your team review and call out any module contract expectations (imports/outputs) and a short checklist we can add to our pipeline?

Thanks,
Ellen
Ellen Cheng
Platform Engineer, Acme Corp

Ellen — thanks for the packet and the clear ask. Quick read-through notes before a deeper pass: 

- High level looks reasonable for brownfield (overlay avoids VLAN churn). A few immediate flags: BGP import/export rules need explicit route-targets per VRF and a deny-by-default import policy on the fabric routers to avoid leaks.
- CI: we want a deterministic terraform plan step plus a policy-as-code (OPA) check on plan JSON; helm should run "helm template" + chart tests (if available) rather than a full cluster apply for the gating stage.

I'll carve out time tomorrow to annotate the terraform plan diff. @kimberly_park -- mind if you particularly look at the KMS/secret paths (we need to ensure sealed-secrets aren't embedding plaintext in CI logs)? @vivek_kulkarni -- can you surface any Dedicated/Private runtime constraints (eg allowed egress IP ranges, NAT gateway patterns) that should be in the module contract?

Next steps: I will send a checklist and a minimal CI workflow example (GitLab) that you can adapt. If you can share the module registry links (module source refs), that will speed the import-safety checks.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Staff SRE (Private Deployments), Redwood Inference

Ellen — appreciated. I did a pass on the plan and pulled out a short, actionable checklist you can fold into your CI as gate steps. Paste below (also adding to the Drive link).

Minimal IaC/CI golden-path checklist (recommended):
1) Terraform: terraform init -> terraform plan -out=plan.tfout -> terraform show -json plan.tfout | opa eval --input - --data infra-policies/rego 'data.terraform.allow' ; fail on policies.
2) Terraform imports: add explicit import tests for any pre-existing resources (e.g., colo subnets, vlan-ids) so plan won't try to recreate. Document import commands in module README.
3) BGP/VRF: require route-target tags in module variables and add fabric-router ACL module that defaults to deny-all-import. Provide an automated test that tries to advertise a cross-tenant prefix and validates it's rejected.
4) Secrets: CI must never echo secrets. Use Vault session tokens with limited TTL and role-scoped policies; ensure terraform plan logs are sanitized (use TF_LOG=ERROR in the pipeline and redact outputs).
5) Helm: run helm lint && helm template --values acme-helm-values.yaml | kubetest (or kubeconform) for schema validation as a gate. Do not apply in gate stage.
6) Observability hooks: module outputs should include tracer endpoints and metrics labels so CI smoke tests can validate endpoint registration post-deploy.
7) Rollback and roll-forward: add a dry-run deployment job that runs in a staging namespace and an automated rollback step if the smoke test fails.

I will follow up with a sample GitLab CI YAML and a small OPA policy example for your team to drop into infra-policies. If you can run the terraform plan with the deny-by-default policy and re-submit the diff, we'll re-run the policy checks and do a short call to sign-off.

If your NetOps folks want to be on the call, loop them in (cc'd).

— Jonas
